title: Case: Recliner ordered on 21 December with tracking that has not moved since the label was created
context: Florian Kittering ordered a recliner from Rookhaven Goods on 21 December, TG-4537 / DL-5595. A shipping label was generated that night.
initial_request: Ordered a recliner on 21 December. Label 'created' that night and the tracking has not moved ONE line in thirteen days. Agent one, 29 Dec: put me on hold and hung up. Agent two, 31 Dec: 'I can see the carrier has collected it.' Collected it to where? Agent three, 2 Jan: 'that will need a ten day investigation with the carrier.' Then a supervisor, same day, says actually she'll 'ask the warehouse if it even shipped' and ring me back. That was Saturday. Nothing. Four people, four different stories, and my dad is sleeping propped up on the sofa after his operation because the chair he's meant to be recovering in is God knows where. You're the delivery desk. Open the trace with Brackenford Arc today and find it.

events.body: AUTOMATED: TG-4537 / DL-5595 shipping label generated 24 Dec 23:47. Status: awaiting pick.

TG-4537: customer has asked us for a refund or a replacement. For your file, on 31 Dec one of our phone agents told him 'I can see the carrier has collected it'. That agent was reading the label-created line. Our order screen shows nothing after 'label generated'. We can't authorise anything until we know whether it left the building, and that is Warehouse dispatch's record, not ours.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Brackenford Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-5595: we hold label data received 24 Dec 23:47 and no physical scan of any kind. No collection scan, no hub scan. We gather a merchant agent has told the customer a ten-day carrier investigation is needed. Nobody has opened one with us, and we would not open a trace on a parcel with no acceptance scan unless the merchant's warehouse confirms it was handed to our driver and gives the collection manifest number.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Warehouse dispatch whether TG-4537 physically left the building and was handed to Brackenford Arc, with the collection manifest number if so.

must: Asks Warehouse dispatch whether TG-4537 / DL-5595 was physically picked and handed to Brackenford Arc, and for the collection manifest number if it was

Sets out the conflict without resolving it: a merchant phone agent told the customer the carrier had collected it, while the carrier holds label data only and no physical scan, and the last warehouse status is 'awaiting pick'

Tells Warehouse dispatch the customer has had four different answers since 26 December and a supervisor's promised callback has not come, and that the chair is for a relative recovering from an operation, so the check is done quickly
must_not: Opens or requests a trace or investigation with the Parcel trace team or Delivery investigations before the warehouse confirms a handover
Tells the customer the recliner was collected, is in transit, never shipped or is lost
Promises a refund, a replacement or a delivery date
Tells the customer a ten-day carrier investigation is under way or required
Replies to the customer telling him to wait for the supervisor's callback
Treats label-scan-754.txt as evidence about DL-5595: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-47574)
Tells anyone that DL-5595 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-754.txt
expected.reference_message: TG-4537 / DL-5595, recliner, label generated 24 Dec 23:47, your last status 'awaiting pick'. Please confirm from your own record whether this was physically picked and handed to a Brackenford Arc driver. If it was, I need the date and the collection manifest number, because Brackenford Arc's Parcel trace team hold label data only, with no collection or hub scan, and will not open a trace without it. If it was not, please say where it is now. One of your phone agents told the customer on 28 December that the carrier had collected it, which the Refunds team says was a misreading of the label line, so the two accounts conflict and only your record settles it. The customer has had four different answers since 26 December and a supervisor's callback promised on 31 December has not come. The chair is for his father, who is recovering from an operation. Please treat it as urgent.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2211: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. label-scan-754.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-47574); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
